                    ### Question
                    Maturity Onset Diabetes of the Young (MODY) type 2 is a consequence of a defective pancreatic enzyme, which normally acts as a glucose sensor, resulting in a mild hyperglycemia. The hyperglycemia is especially exacerbated during pregnancy. Which of the following pathways is controlled by this enzyme?

                    ### Options
                    opa. Glucose --> glucose-6-phosphate
opb. Glucose-6-phosphate --> fructose-6-phosphate
opc. Fructose-6-phosphate --> fructose-1,6-biphosphate
opd. Glyceraldehyde-3-phosphate --> 1,3-bisphosphoglycerate
ope. Phosphoenolpyruvate --> pyruvate

### Enhanced Information (For Contextual Support):
Maturity Onset Diabetes of the Young (MODY) type 2 is caused by a mutation in the glucokinase enzyme, which acts as a glucose sensor in pancreatic beta cells. This enzyme is responsible for the phosphorylation of glucose to glucose-6-phosphate, the first step in glycolysis. This step is crucial for glucose sensing and regulation of insulin secretion. The retrieved evidence paths, while broad, support the role of glucokinase as a glucose sensor interacting with glucose. Therefore, the pathway controlled by this enzyme is the conversion of glucose to glucose-6-phosphate, aligning with option 'opa'.
